scope: Read-only current installed call-order and bounded repair design review; no source/outcome qualification
observedCallOrder: HTTP router resolves method/path and parses allowed media/body, then runs global originCheckMiddleware before the wrapped auth endpoint. This global origin guard checks cookie requests and callbackURLs; cookie-free headerless requests may be admitted.
toAuthEndpoints invokes the application before-hook before endpoint body schema validation and endpoint middleware. Before-hook errors bypass the after-hook.
Application current before-hook can write ACCOUNT_LOCKED audit for future locks and unlock/reset an expired lock before endpoint formCsrfMiddleware.

signInEmail endpoint validates body and runs exported formCsrfMiddleware before credential lookup/verification. The middleware rejects actual cross-site form navigation and validates Origin for cookie/Fetch Metadata requests; existing native cookie-free/headerless calls remain admitted.
Endpoint APIErrors are caught by toAuthEndpoints and passed to application after-hook as context.returned; before-hook failures and ordinary thrown infrastructure errors follow distinct paths.
Application current after-hook classifies every non-success as password failure, so origin/validation/unverified/session-creation errors are not distinguished.
minimalRepairRecommendations: Run the installed exported formCsrfMiddleware at the beginning of the credential-specific before-hook, before any account audit/write; do not reimplement origin matching or disallow supported native clients.
Remove expired-lock reset writes from before-hook; defer reset to a recognized actual credential outcome. This also avoids an expired reset before body validation or infrastructure failure.

Treat only an admitted successful credential result and SDK401 INVALID_EMAIL_OR_PASSWORD as eligible for credential bookkeeping; other APIErrors/transport/validation/unverified/session-creation outcomes must not mutate failure state or report a wrong password.

For recognized wrong password after an expired lock, preserve prior semantics deliberately: reset old expired counter, unlock/null lockedUntil, then record first failure; successful sign-in resets and records success as before.

Keep current-session protection and anonymous recovery flows unchanged. Future-lock legitimate audit behavior must remain intentional, with early origin admission ensuring rejected-origin requests do not reach it.
requiredSourceTests: Origin/metadata rejection before all account writes/audits, including future and expired locks.
Validation, email-unverified, session-creation/infrastructure and unrelated errors no-op credential failure bookkeeping.
Successful sign-in, actual wrong password, threshold transition, expired-lock successful and failed credentials, inactive/indefinite/future locks.
Recognized SDK APIError status/code shape and unsupported/malformed outcomes fail closed for bookkeeping; current-session regression suites remain passing.
nativeRequirements: Actual cross-site form and simple CORS requests with no cookies; persist actual Origin/Fetch Metadata/status/private-byte evidence and native before/after deltas.
Distinct fresh account state per active/threshold/expired-lock/future-lock probe; demonstrate no lock/unlock/counter/audit change on rejected requests.
Wrong/unknown-password origin probes and repeated requests near threshold; legitimate wrong-password and success controls with explicit UTC interpretation and actual bounds.
Rebuild a new source-bound artifact after repair; requalify inherited denial and browser consumer contracts against it.
limits: This inspection establishes current source order; unexercised expired-lock/threshold impacts are source predictions until actual tests.
The already confirmed E29 actual bookkeeping defect remains in immutable r1 evidence.
No new business-policy gate is inferred from a valid-credential nonbrowser API client.
Concurrency/lost-update behavior outside this bounded request-admission repair is not certified.
